articles.title: Settings: Nib
articles.summary: How much Nib says, what he may bring up by himself, his name and colours, and every lesson to start again.
articles.keywords: nib robot helper assistant lesson lessons tutorial tour again restart help first time tips work progress slow struggling sweat lighter display name colour color eyes shell off quiet chatty
articles.body:
Nib is the robot at the top of the window. He is not there while nothing is going on. He comes out of the top edge as a slim line when something is under way or waiting, and opens into a card when there is something to read or answer.

## Presence

- **Quiet** (the default): only when needed. Work that takes longer than a moment, lessons, the first time you open a workspace, and when something went wrong.
- **Chatty**: also a word on your firsts (your first part, your first drawing) and a sleepy face after a long break.
- **Off**: he is not loaded at all.

## What he brings up by himself

Each of these can be switched off on its own:

- **Work under way**: opening a project, an import, an export or a long rebuild, with how far along. A click on the line lists everything that is running.
- **When the machine struggles**: if the view stays slow for several seconds he sweats and offers a **Lighter display**, which draws curves with fewer facets and the panels without blur (Solid glass). The model itself is not changed. **Not now** keeps him quiet about it for twenty minutes.
- **First-time help**: the lesson for a workspace, offered once, the first time you open it.
- **A word on your firsts**: Chatty only.

## Look

His **name**, the colour of his **eyes** and of his **shell**. The head beside the fields shows the result at once.

## Lessons

Every lesson, with how long it takes, marked when you have done it. **Start** begins it now; the first lesson opens a new project for it.

A lesson is never lost to a click elsewhere. **Esc** or the arrow at its top folds it into the line at the top of the window, which says which step you are on; a click opens it again. Only its **×** ends it. **First-time help, Reset** offers each workspace's lesson again the next time you open it.

articles.title: Settings: Viewport
articles.summary: Choose how finely curves are drawn, and how sharp the view stays while you move it.
articles.keywords: viewport quality tessellation resolution smooth smoothness curves facets performance speed fps precision balanced sharp lag slow large model
articles.body:
Settings, Viewport is about how the model is drawn on screen.

![](image:page)

## Surface quality

Three choices, each with the display tolerance it gives:

- **Performance**: fast redraw, 0.25 mm.
- **Balanced**: 0.05 mm. This is the default.
- **Precision**: 0.012 mm, for presentation work.

This changes how finely curves are drawn on screen. The saved geometry and its dimensions stay exact, and so do exports. The change applies to the project that is open, which is rebuilt to draw it.

## While moving the view

![](image:slider)

This slider runs from Sharper to Smoother, in steps named Always sharp, Sharp, Balanced, Smooth and Smoothest. The default is Balanced.

A large model turns smoothly at a lower resolution, and is sharp again the moment it stops. Toward Sharper the view keeps more of its detail and may turn less smoothly. Always sharp never lowers the resolution.

The same slider is in the View panel, see [display modes](doc:display-modes). There, **Detail while modelling** is also offered: Automatic draws curves coarser on a model of more than 20,000 faces, and exports always stay full.

> If the model looks faceted, raise **Surface quality**. If it stutters while you turn it, lower it or move the slider toward Smoother.

slider.alt: The slider for how the view behaves while it moves

articles.title: Settings: Shortcuts
articles.summary: See the key for every command, take the keys of another program, and rebind any one.
articles.keywords: shortcuts keyboard keys hotkeys keybindings rebind remap change key conflict reset clear preset fusion solidworks blender freecad autocad onshape inventor sketchup nx
articles.body:
Settings, Shortcuts lists every command that has a key, in groups: Sketch, Constraints, Modeling, View, Edit, Selection and App. Each row shows the key it uses now.

![](image:page)

## Start from another program

1. Under Shortcut preset, open **Keys like**.
2. Choose Native, Fusion 360, SolidWorks, Onshape, Inventor, FreeCAD, Siemens NX, Blender, SketchUp or AutoCAD.

Native is the default. Choosing a preset throws away any keys you changed. Some commands have no key in some presets, and their row says None.

## Change one key

1. Click the key button in the row of the command.
2. The button says Press keys… Press the new key, with Shift, Alt or Cmd (Ctrl on Windows and Linux) if you want them.
3. The row now says Changed.

![](image:recording)

Escape cancels without changing anything. Pressing only a modifier does nothing, the recording waits for a real key.

## Remove a key

Click **Clear** in the row. The command then has no key and the row says None. You can still reach the command from the rails.

## Two commands on one key

Nothing stops you giving a key to a second command. Both rows then say "Shares its key with another action". When you press the key, the command that comes first in the list and applies at that moment runs, so the other one rarely runs from the keyboard. Give one of them another key.

![](image:conflict)

The presets themselves never share a key.

## Put keys back

![](image:reset)

- **Reset**, beside a changed key, puts that one command back to the preset's key.
- **Reset All Key Bindings** appears once something is changed. It says how many keys are changed and undoes all of them.

## Always

At the bottom, a list of keys that cannot be changed, such as Enter to finish a sketch, Escape to back out and Alt+Cmd (Ctrl on Windows and Linux) with 1 to 4 to switch workspace.

> While Settings is open, only the Settings key works. Close it to use the rest. Keys are ignored while a text field has focus.

articles.title: Settings: Updates and the channels
articles.summary: See which version of Bezier you have, choose between the stable, beta and alpha channels, and enter an invitation code for alpha.
articles.keywords: updates update version release channel stable beta alpha invitation invite code unlock upgrade install new version switch
articles.body:
Settings, Updates shows the **Installed version**, and the **Channel** you follow.

![](image:page)

## Stable, beta and alpha

- **Stable** is what is finished. It is where Bezier starts.
- **Beta** is for what is new and still being proved, before it is stable. Nothing is held back in it yet.
- **Alpha** is for what has not been used outside the lab, and everything in it reaches a server: Community (lessons, plugins and the leaderboard of a store), plugins in the editor, writing in the wiki, collaboration, and a server of your own. Each carries an **Alpha** mark, and the sidebar says Alpha under the logo.

Each channel includes the ones before it. The switch works at once. Nothing is closed or reloaded: the parts that belong to a channel appear in the sidebar and in Settings, or go. What you set up on alpha, a store's address, an account on a server, installed plugins, is kept for the next time.

## The invitation code

Alpha is by invitation. Choose **Alpha**, paste the code you were sent (it starts with BZ-) and press **Unlock**. The code is checked on this device and nothing is sent anywhere. The row then shows when the invitation ends, and **Remove invitation** takes it away again.

A code that has run out or was withdrawn stops opening alpha, and the app comes back up on beta.

Bezier does not update itself yet. New versions come from the website.

When you report a problem, the version is filled in for you, see [Contribute](doc:settings-contribute).

articles.title: Settings: MCP & Automation
articles.summary: Let an assistant such as Claude read this window and change how it looks, with every change listed and put back with one click.
articles.keywords: mcp model context protocol server automation api agent assistant ai claude tools connect client permissions script pairing code
articles.body:
Settings, MCP & Automation is where an assistant such as Claude may connect to Bezier. MCP is a standard way for an assistant program to read and change something in another program.

![](image:page)

## It starts off

**Let assistants connect** is off. While it is, nothing outside Bezier can reach this window.

## Connecting

Bezier's MCP server runs on your own computer, started by the assistant's program, and prints a pairing code. Turn **Let assistants connect** on, enter the server's address and the code, and press **Connect**. The row under the switch says what is happening: connecting, connected, or why not. Bezier remembers the pair and connects whenever both are open. How to start the server, and the tools it offers: the `docs/mcp` folder of the repository.

## What an assistant can do

- **Read.** The model and its history, the selection, pictures of the model, the controls on screen, the settings and how fast Bezier is running.
- **Change settings.** How Bezier looks and draws: theme, size, density, glass, contrast, motion, labels, curve detail and a few more. Never where data goes, the update channel, your keys or the mouse.
- **Never**, through this connection: your files, other projects or the network.

It works the way you do, on screen, so every step it takes is in the history and can be undone.

## What it did

A change to a setting is said on screen and listed here under **Changed by an assistant**, each with **Put back**. Under **Activity** are the last things it asked this window, with how long each took.

articles.title: Settings: Data & Privacy
articles.summary: See where your projects are kept and how much room they take, and put the settings back.
articles.keywords: data privacy storage local telemetry tracking cloud sync reset defaults restore settings clear disk space
articles.body:
Settings, Data & Privacy says where your work is and lets you reset the settings.

![](image:page)

## Local-first storage

Projects stay in this app's private storage on this device. Nothing is sent anywhere.

- **Telemetry** says None. Bezier does not measure what you do.
- **Storage used** is how much of the browser's storage for Bezier is in use, as the browser reports it. It reads Unavailable if the browser will not say.
- **Cloud sync** says In development. It is not built. To share a project with other people, see [collaboration](doc:collaboration).

## Reset settings

**Restore Bezier defaults** puts every setting back: theme, shortcuts, mouse bindings and the rest. Your projects and modeling data are kept.

1. Click **Reset settings**.
2. Two buttons replace it. Click **Reset all settings** to go ahead, or **Cancel**.
3. The row says Settings reset for a moment.

![](image:reset)

The reset covers the mouse and key bindings as well as the look of the interface.

reset.alt: The reset row asking to confirm

articles.title: Settings: Contribute
articles.summary: Report a problem, suggest an idea, or find the code from inside the app.
articles.keywords: contribute github issue bug report idea feedback feature request code source help broken missing repository pull request
articles.body:
Bezier is not finished, and Settings, Contribute is the shortest way to say what is in your way.

![](image:page)

## Four buttons

![](image:actions)

Each opens GitHub in your browser.

- **Something broke** starts a bug report with sections for what happened, what you expected and the steps. The Bezier version and your system (macOS, Windows or Linux) are filled in.
- **I have an idea** starts a note about what you would like and why, with the same two details.
- **A good first fix** lists small, described problems that are waiting for someone.
- **Read the code** opens the map of the repository.

You need a GitHub account to send a report. Nothing is sent until you submit it there.

## Where it is made

The list below the buttons says which folder of the repository holds which part: the start page and Settings, sketching and the tools, the viewport, the model itself, the geometry engine and Learn. Each row opens that folder on GitHub.

articles.title: Community: the wiki, lessons and plugins
articles.summary: Read and improve the wiki, and browse lessons and plugins other people share, without an account.
articles.keywords: community store lessons plugins docs wiki download install share server extension marketplace leaderboard write article improve address points
articles.body:
Community is part of the alpha channel, which opens with an invitation code: see [Updates](doc:settings-updates). On stable and beta the same page is the wiki alone, see [the wiki](doc:wiki).

Community is the page in the sidebar of the start page, after Learn. It has four parts, chosen at the top: Wiki, Lessons, Plugins and Leaderboard. It opens on the Wiki.

![](image:docs)

## Wiki

These pages are the wiki. The articles that come with Bezier need no store and no network. Type in the search above the list to narrow it, or click an article to read it. Ctrl or Cmd and K finds an article from anywhere. See [search](doc:search).

Press **Collapse** to take the wiki off the page into a window that floats over the app. It stays open when you open a project, so an article can sit beside the model it is about. Drag it by its bar, size it from its corner, and press **Expand** on the start page to put it back.

## Writing in the wiki

Press **Edit** on an article, or **New article** above the list. You write on the article as it will read: type **/** at the start of a line for headings, steps, notes, pictures and keys, and select words to make them bold or a link. Drop or paste a picture anywhere, then press **Arrows** on it to point at what matters. Turn on **Show Markdown** to see and edit the same article as text beside it.

**Publish** puts your version live for everyone at once, as on Wikipedia. Every version is kept: **History** on an article lists them, and any one can be put back. Publishing needs a token from whoever runs the store, asked for the first time you publish.

## Lessons, Plugins and Leaderboard

These three come from a store, and the store is off until you turn it on. Bezier's own store does not have an address yet, so until you give one, each of the three says that Bezier Community opens with the launch.

![](image:lessons)

If you run a store of your own, or someone gives you the address of theirs:

1. Press Community settings on the page, or open Settings and choose Community. See [open Settings](doc:open-settings).
2. Under Another store, type the Store address and press Use.
3. Turn on Show what other people share, or press Turn on Community on the page. Bezier asks the store what it has. Nothing of yours is sent, and there is no account to make.

Then:

- **Lessons**: press Download on a lesson, then Open. It is on the Learn page from then on. See [learn](doc:learn).
- **Plugins**: press Install, read what the plugin may do, and confirm with Install. Installed plugins are listed at the top of the page, where each can be switched off or removed. Remove asks once.

> Only a store you choose is asked. A report button on each lesson and plugin tells the store's owner about one that should not be there.

articles.summary: Every article of Bezier in one place: search it, read it, keep it open beside a model.
articles.keywords: wiki docs help articles manual documentation search read float collapse expand command k
articles.body:
The wiki is these pages. The articles come with Bezier, so they need no network and no account.

1. Open **Wiki** in the sidebar of the start page.
2. Type in the search above the list to narrow it, or click an article to read it. Ctrl or Cmd and K finds an article from anywhere, also inside a project. See [search](doc:search).
3. Press **Collapse** to take the wiki off the page into a window that floats over the app. It stays open when you open a project, so an article can sit beside the model it is about. Drag it by its bar, size it from its corner, and press **Expand** on the start page to put it back.

> Writing and changing articles, and the community's lessons, plugins and leaderboard, are on the alpha channel. See [Updates](doc:settings-updates).

articles.title: Work on one model together
articles.summary: Share a project through a server you run, and work in it at the same time as others.
articles.keywords: collaboration share team together live sync server vault invite multiuser realtime simultaneous coworker
articles.body:
Several people open the same project and see each other's changes as they are made, the way a shared document works. Everyone keeps a full copy on their own machine, so you can keep working without a connection.

Bezier runs no server for you. You run one, or someone gives you access to theirs. What it stores is encrypted before it leaves your machine, so it cannot read your models.

## Turn it on

1. Open Settings, Collaboration, and switch it on.
2. Connect to a server. Choose one of three ways: create an account with the server's address and its enrollment code, join with an invite link, or restore an account from a backup file.
3. Type your name and this machine's name. Others see both, so "Alice on Workshop PC" tells them where you are.

![](image:settings)

Back up your identity once you are connected. It is a file with a passphrase; without it, no one can give you back access to what was shared with you.

## Share a project

1. On the start page, open the menu of a project and choose **Share**.
2. Choose where it goes: on its own, or into a vault you already have. A vault is a group of shared projects with the same people.
3. Press Share. Then invite people: make an invite link and send it, or add someone who is already on the server by their id.

![](image:share)

Each person can **view**, **edit** or **administer** the vault. A read-only link lets someone look without an account.

## Work in it together

A shared project is in everyone's list of projects, marked Shared. Open it like any other. At the top of the model a small bar says **Live** and names who else is in the project, and on which machine.

![](image:live)

Two people changing different things both keep their changes. If both change the very same thing at once, the later change wins. Without a connection, the bar says Offline and your changes wait on your machine until it is back.

## When you do not like a change

Press the bar. It lists the latest changes with who made them.

- **Go back to before** sets the model to how it was before that change. That is a change of your own, so everyone sees it, and Undo brings it back.
- **Branch from before** starts a project of its own from that point, so you can try something else without disturbing the others.

![](image:changes)

On a branch, **Merge** brings what the branch changed into the project it came from, and **Discard branch** throws it away.

> The setup files and a guide for running your own server are in Settings, Collaboration, under Run a server.
